# Results — Study 436 (Moving-Average Envelopes) on real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). One recipe — a percent
**moving-average envelope** (SMA(20) ± 5%) turned into a daily **long/flat** timing rule
(buy when the close pierces the lower band, exit at the mid), entered with **one execution
lag** (position known at the close of *t* earns the return of *t+1*), charged one-way costs
× NAV, and raced **excess-of-cash vs excess-of-cash** against buy-and-hold — then pitted
against the two obvious simpler benchmarks, a **Bollinger Band** (the same rule, but a
volatility-scaled band) and a bare **SMA(200)** trend filter. As-of **2026-06-23**.
Total-return adjusted (`auto_adjust=True`). Headline tape: **SPY, 1993-01-29 → 2026-06-23
(n = 8,406 daily bars)**; a five-name panel confirms it.*

## Data stamp

| Ticker | Window | n | Fingerprint |
|---|---|--:|---|
| SPY  | 1993-01-29 → 2026-06-23 | 8406 | `8dc1a394508c` |
| QQQ  | 1999-03-10 → 2026-06-23 | 6864 | `5defef71e491` |
| DIA  | 1998-01-20 → 2026-06-23 | 7150 | `3b6a03746545` |
| IWM  | 2000-05-26 → 2026-06-23 | 6556 | `3b3b482757a0` |
| EFA  | 2001-08-27 → 2026-06-23 | 6241 | `7bdba481585e` |

Prices are total-return adjusted, so every Sharpe below is **net of cost, excess-of-cash,
total-return**. The in-progress 2026-06-24 bar is dropped (no partial day in a stamped run).

## The headline race — SPY, envelope vs the benchmarks (net of 1 bp one-way, excess-of-cash)

| Strategy | ann. Sharpe | HAC *t* | CAGR | max DD | time in market | turnover/yr |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **MA envelope (SMA20 ±5%, buy-the-dip)** | **+0.278** | **+1.97** | +2.45% | −33.2% | 6.6% | 2.6 |
| Bollinger (SMA20 ±2σ, same rule) | +0.444 | +3.11 | +4.86% | −37.0% | 19.0% | 9.0 |
| SMA(200) trend filter | +0.727 | +4.51 | +8.32% | −28.3% | 75.3% | 6.4 |
| **Buy-and-hold** | **+0.644** | +4.33 | +10.78% | −55.2% | 100% | 0.0 |

- The envelope's net Sharpe is **+0.278 at HAC *t* = +1.97** — **below the *t* ≥ 2 bar**,
  so the timing edge is *not* certified by this tape.
- **It does not beat Bollinger Bands.** The volatility-scaled band earns **+0.444** (*t* =
  +3.11) on the same rule, instrument and window — the fixed-percent envelope is the
  *weaker* of the two, answering the headline question directly: **no**.
- Both bands are **dominated by buy-and-hold** (+0.644) and by a trivial SMA(200) filter
  (+0.727). The envelope is in the market only **6.6% of the time** — its "edge" is mostly
  *not being exposed*, i.e. diluted beta with a worse risk-adjusted return than just holding.

## The decisive arbiter — block-permutation placebo (does the *band* time anything?)

We chop the envelope's realised position path into 21-day blocks and shuffle the block
order — destroying the band's specific timing while **preserving the marginal long-fraction**
(same exposure, same in-market autocorrelation). If the band carries information, the real
Sharpe should sit in the right tail of the scrambled distribution.

| | real Sharpe | mean of scrambled | *p*-value |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Envelope (SMA20 ±5%) | +0.278 | +0.168 | **0.232** |

**p = 0.232** — nearly a quarter of randomly mis-timed paths with the *same exposure* match
or beat the real envelope. The band adds no statistically reliable timing information over
"be long this fraction of the time." This is the cleanest evidence the signal is exposure,
not the envelope.

## Cost sweep (SPY, envelope reversion) — costs are *not* the killer

| one-way cost | net Sharpe | HAC *t* | CAGR |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.0 bp (gross) | +0.281 | +1.99 | +2.48% |
| 0.5 bp | +0.279 | +1.98 | +2.47% |
| 1.0 bp | +0.278 | +1.97 | +2.45% |
| 2.0 bp | +0.276 | +1.96 | +2.43% |
| 5.0 bp | +0.269 | +1.91 | +2.35% |

Turnover is low (~2.6 round-trips/yr), so costs barely move the needle. The problem is not
costs — it is that the gross edge never clears the bar and never beats just holding.

## Panel — the picture is the same across five index tapes (net 1 bp)

| Ticker | envelope Sharpe (*t*) | Bollinger Sharpe (*t*) | buy-and-hold Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY | +0.278 (+1.97) | +0.444 (+3.11) | +0.644 |
| QQQ | +0.241 (+1.58) | +0.267 (+1.76) | +0.517 |
| DIA | +0.133 (+0.97) | +0.293 (+1.94) | +0.563 |
| IWM | +0.265 (+1.53) | +0.230 (+1.31) | +0.474 |
| EFA | +0.222 (+1.49) | +0.246 (+1.55) | +0.404 |

No tape clears *t* = 2 on the envelope; **buy-and-hold beats every band on every tape**; and
Bollinger beats the envelope on four of five.

## The breakout reading is worse

Flipping the rule to "buy when the close pierces the *upper* band (trend confirmed)" makes it
worse still: SPY envelope-breakout net Sharpe **+0.116** (*t* = +0.78), Bollinger-breakout
**+0.156** (*t* = +0.98). Neither band-direction earns its keep.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery works when there's something to find

On a deterministic synthetic tape (`data.synthetic_panel`) whose *log price* is a slow drift
plus a mean-reverting deviation (an OU/AR(1) on the level, `edge` = reversion speed), the same
engine recovers a real envelope edge **only when reversion is planted**, with the permutation
placebo confirming it:

| planted `edge` | envelope net Sharpe | placebo *p* | edge detected? |
|---|--:|--:|:--:|
| 0.00 (random walk) | +0.107 | 0.624 | no |
| 0.02 | +0.336 | 0.206 | borderline |
| 0.05 | +0.780 | **0.001** | yes |
| 0.10 | +0.704 | **0.000** | yes |

At `edge = 0` the placebo cannot tell the rule from mis-timed exposure (*p* = 0.62); plant a
mean-reverting deviation and the envelope banks it (*p* → 0.00). The harness is faithful — the
real-tape `p = 0.232` is therefore a statement about **the market** (large-cap index prices
do not mean-revert around their 20-day average on a tradable horizon), not the method.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Net Sharpe **+0.278**, HAC *t* **+1.97** (below the *t* ≥ 2 bar), and a
  block-permutation placebo *p* = **0.232**: the percent envelope adds no reliable timing
  information over the same exposure mis-timed at random. No panel tape clears *t* = 2.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The rule is in the market 6.6% of the time and earns a +0.278
  Sharpe — *worse* risk-adjusted than buy-and-hold (+0.644) and a bare SMA(200) (+0.727). It
  is diluted beta, not alpha; costs are irrelevant because the gross never beats holding.
- **Beats Bollinger Bands? — BUSTED.** On the same rule/instrument/window the
  volatility-scaled Bollinger band earns **+0.444** vs the envelope's **+0.278**, and beats
  it on four of five panel tapes. The fixed-percent envelope is the *weaker* of the two — the
  folk claim that percent envelopes are the better band is not supported.
